name: What if you want to change the floor plan after framing starts?

mainEntity.name: What if you want to change the floor plan after framing starts on a custom home?
mainEntity.text: What if you want to change the floor plan after framing starts on a custom home?

acceptedAnswer.text: Changing the floor plan after framing starts is possible, but it is usually expensive and disruptive. Even a small adjustment can affect structural framing, electrical and plumbing rough-ins, insulation, drywall, cabinetry, and inspections. The builder should document the change, price it as a formal change order, and explain how much time it adds to the schedule before any work proceeds. In custom homes, late changes often cost more than homeowners expect because trades may already be scheduled and materials may already be ordered. In Los Angeles, where permit and inspection timing can already stretch the schedule, late changes can create a chain reaction that delays multiple phases. Homeowners should ask whether the new idea is worth the cost and whether it can be achieved another way with less disruption. The best strategy is to make as many decisions as possible before framing begins.
